#73Linux (Pi aarch64 fork, Arch / pacman branch)
# I want to stress, I am in no way, shape, or form, a programmer. This was generated by grok-ai by pulling KM4ACK's 73Linux Git and updating the script to be used on CM5/Debian Trixie. KM4ACK dropped support for Raspberry Pi's, with more desire to work on x86_64 systems. 73Linux is great for the ClockworkPi uConsole for a portable Station, using a Xeigu X6200 or a QRP-Labs QMX. It also makes quick deployment on a portable ARM device amazing. Scrutinize this as much as possible. Please fork, optimize, and take it further for yourself and those with Raspberry Pi based Radio Go-Bags.



**This `arch-pacman` branch is for Arch-based aarch64 systems (Arch Linux ARM, Manjaro ARM, ...) on a Raspberry Pi 5 / CM5.** It installs with `pacman` and `yay` (AUR) only and never calls apt. It is **not** for Debian / Raspberry Pi OS Trixie; use the `trixie-all-apps` branch for that. Official 73Linux dropped Pi support in 4.1.9. Read ARCH.md first.

## Description

This branch supports Raspberry Pi (aarch64) on Arch-based distributions. You choose which ham radio applications to install.

This is an **unofficial fork**. Original project: [km4ack/73Linux](https://github.com/km4ack/73Linux) by Jason Oleham, KM4ACK.

# Install on a Pi (Arch Linux ARM / Manjaro ARM)

```bash
sudo pacman -Syu
sudo pacman -S --needed git base-devel yad jq bc curl wget
# yay for AUR packages (js8call, trustedqsl, xastir, cqrlog, ...)
git clone https://aur.archlinux.org/yay.git /tmp/yay && (cd /tmp/yay && makepkg -si --noconfirm)
sudo usermod -aG uucp,lock,audio "$USER"
# log out / reboot

git clone -b arch-pacman https://github.com/CzarD0mn/73Linux-pi5-trixie.git $HOME/73Linux-pi5-trixie
bash $HOME/73Linux-pi5-trixie/bootstrap.sh
# 73Linux is installed to your user home, e.g. /home/pi/73Linux
bash $HOME/73Linux/73.sh
```

Keep `.pi5-trixie-fork` in the tree so 73.sh does not replace itself with upstream.
